newsitem.title: USA: Denver summit will be Yeltsin's fifth G7 meeting.
newsitem.headline: Denver summit will be Yeltsin's fifth G7 meeting.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's presence at the June 20-22 summit in Denver of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations will mark the fifth time he has attended such a meeting.
Yeltsin, who missed last year's gathering in Lyon, France, because of ill health, will take part in every meeting at Denver except one, a Saturday afternoon session on economic and financial issues.
Below is a chronology of Soviet and Russian participation in the annual summits of the Group of Seven (G7), which groups Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
July 1991
G7 invites then Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev to its annual summit in London but only for lunch after the conclusion of regular working sessions.
The meeting, the first to which G7 leaders have invited a Soviet leader, gives no tangible support to Gorbachev in the form of economic aid.
July 1992

Russian President Boris Yeltsin attends parts of G7 summit in Munich, enjoying two meals with the leaders and winning $1.5 billion in economic aid as well as a promise to begin talks on rescheduling Russia's massive foreign debt.
July 1993
Yeltsin comes to Tokyo G7 summit, which establishes a $3 billion fund to help Russia privatise its large, state-owned companies and sets up a G7 liaison office in Moscow to coordinate aid.
July 1994
At Naples, Italy, Yeltsin takes part for the first time in the G7 summit's decision-making meetings on political issues.
The summit does not come up with a new aid package for Russia but backs efforts to increase the amount of money the International Monetary Fund can lend the country.
June 1995

At Halifax, Canada, Yeltsin tells G7 leaders he expects the Russian economy to come out of its deep tailspin later in the year, and he is rebuked by his counterparts for Russia's then six-month-long war in Chechnya.
June 1996
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin takes Yeltsin's place at summit in Lyon, France, because of the Russian leader's ill health.

Yeltsin's well-being is a matter of much discussion at the summit, with Chernomyrdin saying publicly that Yeltsin is not seriously ill. Later in the year, Yeltsin is diagnosed with pneumonia and also undergoes quintuple bypass surgery.
June 1997
Yeltsin is scheduled to attend G7 summit in Denver, which the host, the United States, has baptised the "Summit of the Eight" to reflect Russia's expanded role.
The Russian leader is to take part in every meal and meeting at the summit except for Saturday afternoon's session focusing on financial and economic issues.
